notes: Cloudflare launch tables for Clef and Clef-flash (2026-10-01): VENDOR-RUN by Cloudflare, including the Jev, DiffusionGemma Jev, Kev 9B and Laya columns. Quality rows are the "Decision Index 0.2.1 suite ... our internal run" (HF card, all 41 benchmark rows) and the 10 benchmarks the blog shortlisted (2-decimal values; where the card prints a different 1-decimal figure the blog value is kept and the difference is listed in notes). The board mirror marks Clef rows self-reported. Latency rows (209.3/38.8/524.1 ms) carry NO measurement context: hardware, region, payload and percentile procedure are unstated, and the Jev figure is a hosted-HTTPS round trip copied from the third-party Decision Index board, so the 2.5x/13x "faster than Jev" claim compares different quantities (see caveats). Only Clef and Clef-flash numbers are Cloudflare-measured; no independent party reproduced the latencies. Accuracy rows reproduce on the live index within 1 point except suite revisions (GSM8K, Home appliances dedup, BRIGHT subset). Blog (2-decimal) vs HF card (1-decimal) disagreements above 0.05: ToolRet (nDCG@10)/Laya: blog 12.69 vs card 12.8; API-Bank (accuracy)/Laya: blog 11.41 vs card 11.5.

claims.statement: Cloudflare: "Across 10 decision benchmarks, a Clef model scores highest on 7, ahead of Jev and other open decision models." The 10 are a shortlist chosen by Cloudflare; Jev tops When2Call and BRIGHT, DiffusionGemma Jev tops PhishNChips. On the full 41-benchmark HF card table (a Clef model beats Jev on 29 of 41) Jev beats both Clef models on 11 rows (e.g. GPQA Diamond 78.3 vs 48.0, MMLU-Pro 82.7 vs 65.9, BBH 92.9 vs 73.7, When2Call 81.0 vs 72.4, ANLI, HoVer, VAST, NLI4CT, POP909-CL, New Yorker).
claims.implication: Read the 7-of-10 as a vendor-chosen task mix. Clef wins on tool-name selection and fine-grained intent; Jev wins on reasoning-heavy and when-to-call tasks.

claims.statement: Cloudflare: "Clef is currently the leader when evaluated against the Jev Decision Index." The claim dates to the public-only 0.2.1 edition (Clef 61.98 against a top of 57.44 on the 2026-09-28 board snapshot, which did not list Clef). On Decision Index 0.3 public Clef is rank 3 (Torchcast 65.10 is rank 1) and on the 0.3 Full score Clef is rank 19 and Jev rank 3 (see the Decision Index docs).

Cloudflare: "Across our 43 benchmark runs, we achieved speeds where Clef is 2.5x faster than Jev at the median, and Clef-flash 13x faster." 2.5x = 524.1/209.3 and 13x ~ 524.1/38.8 (13.5). The numerator is a hosted HTTPS round trip from a third-party lab; Cloudflare states no condition for 209.3 and 38.8.
claims.implication: Do not use these ratios as a speed claim.

claims.statement: Cloudflare anecdote: a domain classification with Browser Run took Clef 2.2 s to "fetch, render, and classify" versus 4.7 s for gpt-oss-120b in the same workflow (blog). End-to-end workflow time including fetch and render; not a decision latency.

Cloudflare "Hosting on Workers AI adds to that speed. Requests run on GPUs across Cloudflare's network, running close to your users" (changelog); no hosted measurement is given. Independent hosted measurements (OpenRouter p50 Clef 0.51 s, Clef-flash 0.17 s; Requesty; Nicia) are in their own docs.

Cloudflare mirror board caption: "Clef scores and latency are self-reported (missing benchmarks scored 0; latency not measured on the board's hardware)". Its leaderboard.json also contains alternate "price scenario" rows with unexplained different scores; those are not ingested.
